title: थारु जातिको शैक्षिक अवस्था बर्दिया जिल्ला,शिवपुर गाविसको अध्ययन {Educational status of Tharu caste Study of Shivpur VDC, Bardia District}
nepali: त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय, मानविकी र सामाजिकशास्त्र सङ्काय,समाजशास्त्र÷मानवशास्त्र विषयको स्नातकात्तर तह , दोस्रो बर्षको शोध–पत्र  को पाठ्य (S.A 508) क्रमको आवश्यकता पूरा गर्नका लागि यो शोधपत्र ूथारु जातिको शैक्षिक अवस्थाू बर्दिया जिल्ला शिवपुर गाविसको अध्ययन, वीरेन्द्रनगर बहुमुखी क्याम्पस, सुर्खेतमा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । थारु समुदाय तराईका आदिवासी , सुरुमा धर्ती खन्ने ूधर्तीपुत्रू भएर पनि मूलधारमा समायोजन हुन नसकिरहेको यथार्थलाई वास्तविक र सूक्ष्मरूपमा खोतल्ने र विश्लेषण गर्ने हेतुले शोधपत्रको शीर्षक ूथारु जातिको शैक्षिक अवस्थाू छनौट गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनको  उद्देश्यहरुमा ः थारु जातिको शैक्षिक अवस्थाको पहिचान र विश्लेषण गर्नु, थारु जातिको सामाजिक अवस्था र शिक्षाको सम्बन्ध उल्लेख गर्नु,  थारु जातिको शैक्षिक समस्याहरु पत्ता लगाउनु र थारु जातिको शैक्षिक समस्या समाधानका उपायहरू खोजी गर्नु  राखिएको छ । अध्ययन  क्षेत्रमा थारु जातिको बाहुल्याता रहेको पश्चिमी तराईको बर्दिया जिल्लाको मध्य खण्डमा पर्ने शिवपुर गाविसलाई लिइएको छ । अध्ययनलाई ब्यवस्थित र सरल बनाउन शोधपत्रलाई ६ खण्डमा संरचित गरिएको छ ः भाग १ परिचय , भाग २ सान्दर्भिक साहित्यको समीक्षा, भाग ३ शोध विधि, भाग ४ अध्ययन क्षेत्रको परिचय , भाग ५ तथ्यांङ्क विश्लेषण र प्रस्तुतीकरण र भाग ६ मा प्राप्ति , निष्कर्ष र सुझावहरु राखिएको छ । शोधपत्रका उद्देश्यहरु पूरा गर्नका लागि उद्देश्यसंग सम्बन्धित तथ्यांङ्कहरु सङ्कलन गरी सान्दर्भिक साहित्य ,अनुसन्धान र लेखहरुसंग तुलनात्मक विश्लेषण गरी तथ्याङ्कशास्त्रका विधिहरुको प्रयोगद्धारा श्रृंखलाबद्धरूपमा अथ्र्याइएको छ ।  थारु समुदायको विद्यामान शैक्षिक अवस्थालाई हेर्दा–शिक्षाप्रति सकारात्मक धारणा र चेतनाको विकास हुन नसकेको, पढाइलाई भन्दा कामलाई प्राथमिकता दिएको, घरमा शैक्षिक वातावरण नभएको,बालबालिकाहरूमाथि अभिभावकले निगरानी नराखेको , खानपिन र मोजमस्तिमा रमाइरहेको जस्ता पक्षहरु पाइयो । थारु समुदायका शैक्षिक समस्याहरुमा–गरिबीका कारण अरूको काम गर्नु पर्ने बाध्यता ,परम्परादेखि नै सोझा,शोषणमा परेका र सुबिधाविहीन बर्गका रूपमा जीवन गुजारीरहेका ,खानपिन र मोजमस्तिमा रमाई आफ्नो पहिचान नखोजिरहेका, गैर–थारु शिक्षकका कारण भाषिक समस्या परेको ,शिक्षिका नहँुदा छात्रा भर्नामा कमी भएको, राज्यसरकारले वास्तविक रुपमा उकास्ने दृढता नदेखाई अलमल्याउने नीति अनुरूप केही अवसरहरु दिए जस्तो गरेको , सरकारी तथा गैर–सरकारी संस्थाहरु बीच समन्वयको अभाव र सुगममा मात्र कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गरी दुर्गममा नगरेको ,द्धन्द्धका कारण लक्षित कार्यक्रमहरुले सफलता नपाएको जस्ता कारणहरु पाइयो ।  थारु समुदायका शैक्षिक समस्या समाधानका उपायहरुमा–थारु समुदायले आफ्नो पहिचान खोज्न स्वयम् आफै सक्रिय हुनुपर्ने ,राज्य सरकारले विभेदपूर्ण तथा असमान ऐन ,नियम र कानुनहरूमा सुधार गर्नु पर्ने, सुबिधाविहिन बर्गलाई उकास्न विशेष (Equitable)  लक्षित कार्यक्रमहरु सञ्चालन गर्नुपर्ने ,थारु समुदायलाई सबै पक्षहरुमा अवसर दिनुपर्ने, आफ्नै भाषामा शिक्षा दिन थारु शिक्षकहरुको ब्यवस्था गर्नुपर्ने, छात्रा भर्ना बढाउन शिक्षिकाहरुको ब्यवस्था गर्नुपर्ने जस्ता पक्षहरु औंल्याइएको छ । निष्कर्षमा आफू नमरी स्वर्ग देखिंदैनू भने झं थारु समुदायको विकासमा स्वयम् थारुहरु नै सक्रिय हुनु आवश्यक छ ।अधिकार मागेर होइन खोसेर लिनु पर्दछ । यथास्थिति र भाग्यवादमा नअल्झिइ समयको माग र आवश्यकतानुसार अगाडि बढ्नु अत्यावश्यक छ । प्राकृतिक  स्रोत र साधन सबैका साझा हुन् , सबैले समान  उपभोग गर्न पाउनु मानव अधिकार हो ।
american_english:
In order to fulfill the requirement of the course (S.A. 508) of the second-year research paper at the master's level in the subject of Sociology/Anthropology, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Tribhuvan University, this research paper, 'Educational Status of the Tharu Caste: A Study of Shivpur VDC, Bardia District', has been presented at Birendranagar Multiple Campus, Surkhet.
With the aim of exploring and analyzing, realistically and minutely, the reality that the Tharu community — an indigenous people of the Tarai and, at the outset, 'sons of the soil' who dug the earth — has not been able to be integrated into the mainstream, the title of the research paper, 'Educational Status of the Tharu Caste', has been chosen.
In the objectives of this study, the following have been set: to identify and analyze the educational status of the Tharu caste, to state the relation between the social status of the Tharu caste and education, to find out the educational problems of the Tharu caste, and to search for ways to solve the educational problems of the Tharu caste.
As the study area, Shivpur VDC, which falls in the central section of Bardia district in the western Tarai, where the Tharu caste is in the majority, has been taken.
To make the study organized and simple, the research paper has been structured in 6 parts: Part 1 Introduction, Part 2 Review of the relevant literature, Part 3 Research method, Part 4 Introduction of the study area, Part 5 Analysis and presentation of data, and Part 6 contains the findings, conclusions and suggestions.
In order to fulfill the objectives of the research paper, data related to the objectives were collected, a comparative analysis was made with the relevant literature, research and articles, and an interpretation was given in a connected sequence through the use of statistical methods.
Looking at the existing educational status of the Tharu community, aspects such as a positive attitude toward education and awareness not having developed, priority being given to work over study, the absence of an educational environment at home, parents not keeping watch over the children, and their taking pleasure in food and merrymaking were found.
Among the educational problems of the Tharu community, causes such as the compulsion to work for others because of poverty; living, by tradition, as a simple, exploited and deprived class; taking pleasure in food and merrymaking and not seeking their own identity; linguistic problems arising because of non-Tharu teachers; a decline in girl students' enrollment when there are no female teachers; the state government appearing to give a few opportunities in line with a policy of dithering without showing the determination to uplift them in reality; the lack of coordination between governmental and non-governmental organizations and the running of programs only in accessible areas and not in remote ones; and the targeted programs not achieving success because of the conflict.
Among the ways of solving the educational problems of the Tharu community, aspects such as the Tharu community itself having to be active in seeking its identity; the state government having to reform discriminatory and unequal acts, rules and laws; special (equitable) targeted programs having to be run to uplift the deprived class; the Tharu community having to be given opportunities in all respects; arrangements for Tharu teachers having to be made to provide education in their own language; and arrangements for female teachers having to be made to increase girls' enrollment.
In conclusion, as it is said that one cannot see heaven without dying oneself, the Tharus themselves need to be active in the development of the Tharu community.
Rights have to be taken by snatching, not by asking.
It is essential to move forward according to the demands and needs of the time without being caught up in the status quo and fatalism.
Natural resources and means are common to all; it is a human right that everyone should be able to enjoy them equally.
british_english:
In fulfilment of the requirement of the course (S.A. 508) of the second-year dissertation at postgraduate level in the subject of Sociology/Anthropology, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Tribhuvan University, this research paper, 'The Educational Condition of the Tharu Caste: A Study of Shivpur VDC, Bardia District', has been presented at Birendranagar Multiple Campus, Surkhet.
With the purpose of probing and analysing, truthfully and in fine detail, the reality that the Tharu community — an indigenous people of the Tarai and originally 'sons of the soil' who tilled the earth — has not been able to become integrated into the mainstream, the title of the research paper, 'The Educational Condition of the Tharu Caste', has been selected.
The objectives set for this study are: to identify and analyse the educational condition of the Tharu caste, to set out the relationship between the social condition of the Tharu caste and education, to discover the educational problems of the Tharu caste, and to seek the means of resolving the educational problems of the Tharu caste.
For the study area, Shivpur VDC, lying in the central part of Bardia district in the western Tarai, where the Tharu caste predominates, has been taken.
In order to make the study orderly and straightforward, the research paper has been structured into six parts: Part 1 Introduction, Part 2 Review of the relevant literature, Part 3 Research method, Part 4 Introduction to the study area, Part 5 Analysis and presentation of data, and Part 6, which contains the findings, conclusions and suggestions.
To meet the objectives of the research paper, data bearing on the objectives were gathered, compared and analysed against the relevant literature, research and articles, and interpreted in a systematic sequence by means of statistical methods.
On examining the present educational condition of the Tharu community, the following aspects were found: a positive outlook on education and an awareness that have failed to develop, a preference for work over study, no educational environment in the home, a lack of supervision of the children by parents, and absorption in food and merrymaking.
Among the educational problems of the Tharu community, the following causes were found: the necessity of working for others owing to poverty; a life lived, by tradition, as a simple, exploited and underprivileged class; absorption in food and merrymaking and no search for their own identity; linguistic difficulty caused by non-Tharu teachers; a fall in the enrolment of girls where there are no women teachers; the state government seeming to offer a few opportunities under a policy of prevarication, without showing any real determination to raise them up; the absence of coordination between governmental and non-governmental bodies, and the conduct of programmes only in accessible areas and not in remote ones; and the failure of the targeted programmes to succeed because of the conflict.
Among the means of resolving the educational problems of the Tharu community, the following aspects have been singled out: the Tharu community itself must be active in the search for its identity; the state government must reform discriminatory and unequal acts, rules and laws; special (equitable) targeted programmes must be conducted to raise up the underprivileged class; the Tharu community must be given opportunities in every respect; provision must be made for Tharu teachers so that education may be given in their own language; and provision must be made for women teachers in order to increase the enrolment of girls.
In conclusion, as the saying goes, one cannot see heaven without dying, so the Tharus themselves must be active in the development of the Tharu community.
Rights must be seized, not asked for.
It is essential to press ahead in keeping with the demands and needs of the time, without becoming entangled in the status quo and in fatalism.
Natural resources and means are the common property of all; it is a human right for everyone to be able to enjoy them equally.
australian_english:
To meet the requirements of the course (S.A. 508) for the second-year research paper in the postgraduate program in Sociology/Anthropology, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Tribhuvan University, this research paper, 'Educational Status of the Tharu People: A Study of Shivpur VDC, Bardia District', has been presented at Birendranagar Multiple Campus, Surkhet.
The title of the research paper, 'Educational Status of the Tharu People', was chosen with the aim of digging into and analysing, honestly and closely, the reality that the Tharu community — the indigenous people of the Tarai and, from the start, earth-digging 'sons of the soil' — still has not managed to be brought into the mainstream.
In the objectives of this study, these things have been set down: to work out and analyse the educational status of the Tharu people, to set out the connection between the social situation of the Tharu people and education, to find the educational problems of the Tharu people, and to look for ways to solve the educational problems of the Tharu people.
For the study area, Shivpur VDC has been taken; it sits in the middle section of Bardia district in the western Tarai, where the Tharu people are the majority.
To keep the study orderly and easy to follow, the research paper has been set out in six parts: Part 1 Introduction, Part 2 Review of the relevant literature, Part 3 Research method, Part 4 Introduction to the study area, Part 5 Analysis and presentation of data, and Part 6, where the findings, conclusions and suggestions are placed.
To carry out the objectives of the research paper, data tied to the objectives were gathered, compared against the relevant literature, research and articles, and interpreted in a step-by-step sequence using statistical methods.
Looking at the current educational situation of the Tharu community, aspects such as these turned up: a positive attitude towards education and an awareness that have not developed, priority given to work rather than study, no educational environment at home, parents not keeping an eye on the children, and everyone caught up in food and a good time.
On the educational problems of the Tharu community, causes such as these turned up: having to work for others because of poverty; living, by tradition, as a straightforward, exploited and disadvantaged class; being caught up in food and a good time and not looking for their own identity; language problems brought on by non-Tharu teachers; fewer girls enrolled when there are no female teachers; the state government seeming to hand out a few opportunities under a muddled policy, without any real determination to lift them up; the lack of coordination between government and non-government bodies, and programs run only in easy-to-reach places and not in remote ones; and the targeted programs failing to succeed because of the conflict.
On ways to solve the educational problems of the Tharu community, aspects such as these have been pointed to: the Tharu community itself has to get active in the search for its identity; the state government has to fix discriminatory and unequal acts, rules and laws; special (equitable) targeted programs have to be run to lift up the disadvantaged class; the Tharu community has to be given opportunities on every front; arrangements have to be made for Tharu teachers to teach in their own language; and arrangements have to be made for female teachers to lift girls' enrolments.
In conclusion, as the saying goes, no one sees heaven without dying, so the Tharus themselves need to get active in the development of the Tharu community.
Rights have to be grabbed, not asked for.
It is vital to move ahead with the demands and needs of the time, without getting stuck in the status quo and in fatalism.
Natural resources and means belong to everyone in common; everyone being able to use them equally is a human right.
informal_english:
To tick off the requirement for the course (S.A. 508) in the second-year research paper at the master's level in Sociology/Anthropology, Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Tribhuvan University, this paper, 'Educational Status of the Tharu Caste: A Study of Shivpur VDC, Bardia District', was handed in at Birendranagar Multiple Campus, Surkhet.
We chose the paper's title, 'Educational Status of the Tharu Caste', because we wanted to dig into the reality — honestly and right down to the details — that the Tharu community, the original people of the Tarai and 'sons of the soil' who dug the earth from the start, still hasn't managed to fit into the mainstream.
The study's objectives lay out like this: figure out and analyse where the Tharu caste stands educationally, spell out the link between the Tharu caste's social situation and education, find the educational problems the Tharu caste faces, and hunt for ways to fix those problems.
For the study area we took Shivpur VDC, which sits in the middle chunk of Bardia district in the western Tarai, where the Tharu caste makes up most of the population.
To keep things neat and simple, the paper is split into 6 parts: Part 1 Introduction, Part 2 Review of the relevant literature, Part 3 Research method, Part 4 Introduction to the study area, Part 5 Analysis and presentation of data, and Part 6, which holds the findings, conclusions and suggestions.
To hit the paper's objectives, we gathered data tied to them, weighed it against the relevant literature, research and articles, and laid it out step by step using statistical methods.
Looking at how the Tharu community is doing education-wise right now, we found things like: a positive attitude toward education and awareness not getting off the ground, work coming before school, no educational atmosphere at home, parents not keeping an eye on the kids, and everyone having a grand old time with food and fun.
On the educational problems of the Tharu community, we found causes like: having to work for other people because of poverty; living, as they always have, as a straightforward, exploited and worse-off class; having a grand old time with food and fun and not looking for their own identity; language trouble because of non-Tharu teachers; fewer girls signing up when there are no female teachers; the state government handing out a few chances under a wishy-washy policy without any real backbone to lift them up; government and non-government groups not coordinating, and running programs only in easy-to-reach places and not in the remote ones; and the targeted programs not getting anywhere because of the conflict.
On fixing the educational problems of the Tharu community, we pointed to things like: the Tharu community itself has to get moving to find its identity; the state government has to clean up discriminatory and unfair acts, rules and laws; special (equitable) targeted programs have to be run to lift up the worse-off class; the Tharu community has to get a fair shot on every front; there have to be Tharu teachers so kids can learn in their own language; and there have to be female teachers so more girls sign up.
Bottom line, like the saying goes, you can't see heaven without dying, so the Tharus themselves have to get moving on the Tharu community's development.
Rights aren't something you ask for — you take them.
You can't get stuck on how things are or on fate; you have to move with what the times demand and need.
Natural resources and means belong to everybody; everyone getting to use them equally is a human right.
